readmeHtml:
Cactus Needle has moved

Cactus Needle has moved to cactus-compute/cactus.

Visit the Cactus repository for the code, documentation, releases, and issues.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A 26M parameter Simple Attention Network optimized for function calling.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Needle is a highly compact, 26-million parameter language model tailored specifically for structured function calling. Built on the Simple Attention Network architecture, it is designed for deployment in resource-constrained environments where standard large language models are impractical. It offers extremely fast inference, achieving 6000 tokens per second for prefilling and 1200 tokens per second for decoding when running on Cactus. The model can also be fine-tuned locally on consumer hardware like a standard Mac or PC. It is meticulously optimized for environments with minimal RAM, operating within a few hundred megabytes.
keyFeatures: Ultra-lightweight architecture: utilizes only 26 million parameters to enable execution on minimal consumer hardware.
Function calling focus: trained specifically to parse complex inputs and accurately output structured tool calls.
High-speed inference: achieves exceptionally fast prefill and decode speeds when paired with the Cactus runtime.
Local finetunability: designed so developers can train and adapt the model entirely on personal computers.
Open-weight distribution: provides complete access to model weights and dataset generation scripts on Hugging Face.

useCases.title: On-device tool execution
useCases.description: Developers deploy it on local machines to route natural language to local APIs without cloud latency.

useCases.title: Edge computing automation
useCases.description: Engineers embed the model into edge devices to handle structured JSON outputs locally.

useCases.title: Custom function calling
useCases.description: Researchers fine-tune the model on specific datasets to improve accuracy for proprietary internal tools.

useCases.title: Low-latency parsing
useCases.description: Systems use it to rapidly convert user intent into actionable backend commands.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI developers and researchers who need a fast, local, and lightweight model specifically for translating natural language into function calls. It is especially useful for integration into edge devices or constrained environments where large models are impractical. The focus on function calling ensures reliable interactions with external APIs.
